queries: WITH c AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS copies FROM inventory i JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), a AS (SELECT AVG(copies) AS avg_copies FROM c) SELECT SUM(c.copies) AS total_copies, AVG(c.copies - a.avg_copies) AS avg_excess FROM c CROSS JOIN a WHERE c.copies > a.avg_copies

responses.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS copies FROM inventory i JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), a AS (SELECT AVG(copies) AS avg_copies FROM c) SELECT SUM(c.copies) AS total_copies, AVG(c.copies - a.avg_copies) AS avg_excess FROM c CROSS JOIN a WHERE c.copies > a.avg_copies

assumptions.assumption: Ratings with no inventory copies do not appear; the average is over ratings that have at least one copy. All five ratings have copies in the verified data, so this has no effect.
The average excess is the mean of (rating count minus across-rating average) over only the above-average ratings, unrounded.

assumptions.assumption: Ratings with zero inventory copies would not appear; all 5 ratings have copies, so the across-rating average is over the 5 ratings present.
'Average amount by which their counts exceed the across-rating average' is the mean of (copies - overall average) over the above-average ratings only.

responses.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS copies FROM inventory i JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), avg_c AS (SELECT AVG(copies) AS avg_copies FROM counts) SELECT SUM(c.copies) AS total_copies, AVG(c.copies - a.avg_copies) AS avg_excess FROM counts c CROSS JOIN avg_c a WHERE c.copies > a.avg_copies

assumptions.assumption: The average of the per-rating counts is taken over the 5 ratings that have inventory copies (inner join from inventory to film), so ratings with no copies are not included.
The average excess is the mean of (rating count minus across-rating average) over only the above-average ratings, left unrounded.
